securite.fichiers.pass: No known sensitive file is readable.
securite.fichiers.fail: A sensitive file is readable by everyone.
securite.fichiers.fail_many: {count} sensitive files are readable by everyone.
securite.fichiers.untested: We could not test the sensitive files.
securite.listing.fail: A folder shows the list of its files.
securite.listing.untested: We could not test the folder listing.
securite.tls.pass: The site offers TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3, with no older version.
securite.tls.warn: The site does not offer TLS 1.3. It stays on TLS 1.2.
securite.tls.fail: The site still accepts TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1.
securite.tls.untested: We could not test the encryption versions.
securite.https.pass_redirect: Pages open on an encrypted address, and the old address sends you there.
securite.https.pass_no_http: Pages open on an encrypted address. The old address does not answer.
securite.https.fail: The site opens without encryption. Someone on the network can read the exchange.
securite.https.warn_off_host: The unencrypted address goes to another name. The browser may forget the protection.
securite.https.warn_delayed: The move to the encrypted address is not immediate. The first step stays readable.
securite.hsts.pass: The browser then refuses unencrypted addresses for this site.
securite.hsts.fail_missing: The browser can still try an unencrypted address. The first visit stays exposed.
securite.hsts.fail_invalid: The encryption-duration header cannot be read. The browser ignores it.
securite.hsts.fail_no_https: This protection does not apply: the site has no encrypted address.
securite.hsts.warn_short: Protection against the unencrypted address lasts less than six months.
securite.csp.pass: The site limits where scripts and embedded objects can come from.
securite.csp.fail_missing: No rule limits where scripts come from. A trapped page can load them from elsewhere.
securite.csp.fail_invalid: The script-origin rule cannot be read. The browser ignores it.
securite.csp.fail_unsafe: The rule allows scripts that are too broad. A trapped page can run code.
securite.csp.warn_loose: The rule blocks the riskiest scripts, but it stays too open.
securite.xcto.pass: The browser respects the announced type of each file.
securite.xcto.warn_missing: The browser may guess a file’s type. A download can then run.
securite.xcto.fail: File types are announced with an unknown value. The browser ignores it.
securite.frames.pass: Another page cannot show yours inside a frame.
securite.frames.fail: Another page can show yours inside a misleading frame.
securite.frames.warn_obsolete: The frame ban uses an old spelling. Current browsers ignore it.
securite.referrer.pass: The site limits the address sent when a visitor follows a link.
securite.referrer.pass_absent: No header limits the address sent. Recent browsers already limit it.
securite.referrer.warn_legacy: The full address still goes to other encrypted sites.
securite.referrer.warn_unsafe: The site sends too much of the address to the sites that follow. A link can reveal the page.
securite.referrer.fail_invalid: The header that limits the sent address cannot be read. The browser ignores it.
securite.permissions.pass: The camera, the microphone, and location are refused by default.
securite.permissions.warn_missing: The camera, the microphone, or location can still be requested.
securite.permissions.fail_open: These accesses are open to every site. A frame can ask for the camera, the microphone, or location.
securite.permissions.fail_invalid: The header that sets the camera and the microphone cannot be read. The browser ignores it.
securite.cookies.pass_none: The page leaves no trace on your browser.
securite.cookies.pass: The traces that are left stay encrypted, and page code does not read the session ones.
securite.cookies.warn_hsts: A trace does not require encryption, but the encrypted address is enforced.
securite.cookies.fail_session_secure: A session trace can travel without encryption. Someone on the network can copy it.
securite.cookies.fail_session_httponly: A session trace is readable by page code. A trapped script can take it.
securite.cookies.fail_secure: A trace can travel without encryption. It can be read on the network.
securite.cookies.fail_samesite: A trace can be sent from another site. An action can leave without your gesture.
securite.cookies.fail_prefix: A trace announces a lock that its options contradict. The browser may refuse it.
securite.certificate.pass: The certificate is recognized, in the site’s name, for another {jours} days.
securite.certificate.fail_expired: The certificate is expired. Visitors see a warning and may leave.
securite.certificate.fail_not_yet: The certificate is not valid yet. Visitors see a warning.
securite.certificate.fail_hostname: The certificate does not cover the site name. Visitors see a warning.
securite.certificate.fail_chain: The browser does not recognize the certificate chain. Visitors see a warning.
securite.certificate.warn_soon: The certificate expires in {jours} days. After that date, visitors will see a warning.
securite.certificate.warn_today: The certificate expires in less than a day. Visitors will then see a warning.
securite.mixed.pass: The encrypted page loads nothing from an unencrypted address.
securite.mixed.fail: The encrypted page loads code from an unencrypted address. That code can be changed.
securite.mixed.warn: The encrypted page loads images or media from an unencrypted address.
securite.mixed.na_http: Mixed content does not apply: the page is not encrypted.
securite.mixed.na_not_html: Mixed content is not tested: the response is not HTML.
securite.security_txt.pass: A file says who to contact about a weakness, and it is still valid.
securite.security_txt.fail_missing: No file says who to contact if a weakness is found.
securite.security_txt.fail_invalid: The contact file is incomplete or expired. Nobody knows who to write to.
securite.security_txt.warn_soon: The contact file expires in {jours} days. Renew it before that date.
securite.security_txt.warn_today: The contact file expires in less than a day. Renew it now.
securite.security_txt.warn_legacy: The contact file is at the old address. Put it in the expected folder.
securite.security_txt.warn_type: The contact file is not served as plain text. Some tools will ignore it.
securite.security_txt.warn_canonical: The contact file announces an address other than the one that answers.
securite.security_txt.untested_status: We could not test: the contact file answered {status}.
securite.technologies.pass: Technologies seen: {liste}. No header announces a version number.
securite.technologies.pass_aucune: Neither the server nor the page announces a known technology.
securite.technologies.warn: Headers announce versions: {liste}. That helps target a known weakness. Hide these numbers.
securite.technologies.untested: We could not read the page to spot its technologies.
securite.cve_scripts.fail_kev: Possibly vulnerable version: {liste}. Known weaknesses: {count}, including one exploited according to CISA. Update without waiting.
securite.cve_scripts.fail: Possibly vulnerable version: {liste}. Known weaknesses: {count}, including at least one serious. Update these scripts.
securite.cve_scripts.warn: Possibly vulnerable version: {liste}. Known weaknesses: {count}, of moderate severity. Plan an update.
securite.cve_scripts.pass: Recognized scripts: {liste}. OSV knows no weakness for these versions.
securite.cve_scripts.pass_partiel: Recognized scripts: {liste}. OSV knows no weakness for these versions. Scripts not checked: {count}.
securite.cve_scripts.na_aucun: No known library was seen in the page scripts.
securite.cve_scripts.na_version: Libraries seen without a comparable version: {liste}. Without a sure version, we report no weakness.
securite.cve_scripts.untested_page: We could not read the page, and therefore not its scripts.
securite.cve_scripts.untested_scripts: We could not read every script on the page. No library could be compared.
securite.cve_scripts.untested_source: We could not query the OSV weakness database.
securite.cve_scripts.quota: The OSV weakness database is limiting requests. We could not test these scripts.
securite.cve_scripts.missing_api: We could not test: the connection to the weakness databases is not set up.
securite.cve_logiciels.fail_kev: Possibly vulnerable version: {liste}. Known weaknesses: {count}, including one exploited according to CISA. Update without waiting.
securite.cve_logiciels.fail: Possibly vulnerable version: {liste}. Known weaknesses: {count}, including at least one serious. Update this software.
securite.cve_logiciels.warn: Possibly vulnerable version: {liste}. Known weaknesses: {count}, of moderate severity. Plan an update.
securite.cve_logiciels.warn_distribution: Possibly vulnerable version: {liste}. Your distribution sometimes patches without changing this number. Check its updates.
securite.cve_logiciels.pass: Recognized software: {liste}. No published weakness for these versions.
securite.cve_logiciels.pass_partiel: Recognized software: {liste}. No published weakness for these versions. Software not checked: {count}.
securite.cve_logiciels.na_aucun: The site announces no server software.
securite.cve_logiciels.na_version: Software seen: {liste}. Without a full version or a reliable base, we report no weakness.
securite.cve_logiciels.na_outil: The site is built with {liste}. This tool does not run on the published site.
securite.cve_logiciels.na_hebergeur: The server is managed by {liste}. The host applies its own fixes.
securite.cve_logiciels.untested_page: We could not read the page to spot its software.
securite.cve_logiciels.untested_source: We could not query the NVD and OSV weakness databases.
securite.cve_logiciels.quota: A weakness database is limiting requests. We could not test this software.
securite.cve_logiciels.missing_api: We could not test: the connection to the weakness databases is not set up.

rgesn.intro: These questions complete the automatic measurements. Answer for your service.
rgesn.1.1: Have you weighed the service’s usefulness against its impacts?
rgesn.1.2: Have you described the people aimed at and their real needs?
rgesn.1.3: Is an ecodesign lead named for this service?
rgesn.1.4: Do you regularly review whether your approach is followed?
rgesn.1.5: Have you set targets to reduce impact?
rgesn.1.6: Is data collection limited to what the service needs?
rgesn.1.7: Is encryption proportionate to the service’s needs?
rgesn.1.8: Have you published part of the service as open code?
rgesn.1.9: Does the service rely on open, interoperable standards?
rgesn.1.10: Do exchanges with hardware go through open APIs?
rgesn.2.1: Have you listed the devices that can use the service?
rgesn.2.2: Does the service still work on older devices?
rgesn.2.3: Does the service stay usable on a slow connection?
rgesn.2.4: Does the service work on older systems and browsers?
rgesn.2.5: Does the layout adapt to phone, tablet, and computer?
rgesn.2.6: Do the design and the code aim to reduce impacts?
rgesn.2.7: Have you planned maintenance and the end of the service?
rgesn.2.8: Do your suppliers commit to reducing their impacts?
rgesn.2.9: Have you weighed the impact of ready-made interface components?
rgesn.2.10: Have you weighed the impact of third-party services before choosing them?
rgesn.3.1: Is the architecture designed to limit its own impacts?
rgesn.3.2: Do resources adapt to the service’s real use?
rgesn.3.3: Can the service follow protocol changes?
rgesn.3.4: Are fixes provided for the whole planned lifetime?
rgesn.3.5: Can a fix be installed without a product upgrade?
rgesn.3.6: Do updates send only what changed?
rgesn.3.7: Are test environments used only when needed?
rgesn.4.1: Do videos, sounds, and animations stay stopped at the start?
rgesn.4.2: Does the service avoid endless scrolling of content?
rgesn.4.3: Is each main journey short and direct?
rgesn.4.4: Can the person choose to turn on a third-party service?
rgesn.4.5: Do you mostly use components the platform already provides?
rgesn.4.6: Do videos, sounds, and animations carry useful information?
rgesn.4.7: Do you choose the lightest medium that meets the need?
rgesn.4.8: Is the number of downloaded fonts limited?
rgesn.4.9: Does typing avoid a server request on every keystroke?
rgesn.4.10: Is the expected format shown before the form is sent?
rgesn.4.11: Are the weight and the format of files announced before sending?
rgesn.4.12: Do you warn when a feature has an important impact?
rgesn.4.13: Are notifications rare and can they be turned off?
rgesn.4.14: Does the interface avoid tricks that push more use?
rgesn.4.15: Can the person follow and reduce the impact of their use?
rgesn.5.1: Does each image use a format suited to its content?
rgesn.5.2: Is each image’s compression suited to its use?
rgesn.5.3: Does each video have a definition suited to its display?
rgesn.5.5: Do videos offer listening without the picture?
rgesn.5.6: Is the audio compression suited to listening?
rgesn.5.7: Does each document use a format suited to its use?
rgesn.5.8: Are outdated contents archived or deleted?
rgesn.6.1: Are a maximum weight and a request count set per screen?
rgesn.6.2: Are the contents you control cached on the visitor’s side?
rgesn.6.3: Are the texts you control compressed when sent?
rgesn.6.4: Do images have dimensions close to the display?
rgesn.6.5: Do you avoid loading unused resources?
rgesn.6.6: Are the device sensors turned on only when needed?
rgesn.6.7: Do your static files leave from a single domain name?
rgesn.7.1: Is there a server cache for the most requested data?
rgesn.7.2: Do data have a retention period, then a deletion?
rgesn.7.3: Is a treatment in progress shown, to avoid a double send?
rgesn.7.4: If a blockchain is used, is its consensus sober?
rgesn.8.1: Does the host publish an approach to reduce impact?
rgesn.8.2: Does the host have a durable policy for its equipment?
rgesn.8.3: Is the hosting PUE published and low?
rgesn.8.4: Is the hosting water use tracked and limited?
rgesn.8.5: Is the hosting electricity documented and mostly renewable?
rgesn.8.6: Is the hosting located where electricity is low-carbon?
rgesn.8.7: Is server heat recovered or well controlled?
rgesn.8.8: Are rarely read data separated from active data?
rgesn.8.9: Are data copies limited to what is strictly needed?
rgesn.8.10: Do deferred treatments avoid consumption peaks?
rgesn.9.1: Is training a model really necessary for the service?
rgesn.9.2: Is the learning phase proportionate to real use?
rgesn.9.3: Have you limited the amount of training needed?
rgesn.9.4: Are the training data reduced to what is strictly needed?
rgesn.9.5: Are retraining runs spaced according to real need?
rgesn.9.7: Is inference set to limit the resources used?

a11y.state: State on 24 Oct. 2026: no formal audit has been done.
a11y.goal: The goal is level AA of RGAA 4.1.
a11y.honest: This page does not declare conformity. The audit is still to be done.

method.lead: This page explains how Audigy calculates its scores.
method.change: Any change of weighting creates a new version.
method.recorded: The version is recorded on each audit.
method.status.title: Result of a test
method.warn: Needs work: the point is partial. Value 0.5.
method.fail: Problem: the point does not conform. Value 0.
method.untested: Not tested: the test is impossible, with the reason. It is excluded.
method.na: Not applicable: the test has no object. It is excluded.
method.partial: A test can give a value between 0 and 1.
method.weight: Each test weighs 1, 2, or 3 in its domain.
method.skip.title: When a test becomes not tested
method.skip.lead: The test is not counted, and the reason is shown.
method.skip.active: An active test is never started without ownership checked again.
method.skip.source: The source may be missing: key, quota, or browser.
method.skip.timeout: A timeout makes the test not tested.
method.skip.error: An error during the test has the same effect.
method.passive: A passive test does what a visitor would do.
method.active: An active test requires a verified site.
method.penal: Without a mandate, an active test can be an offense.
method.domain.title: Score of a domain
method.domain.formula: The score rounds 100 times the points obtained, divided by the points possible.
method.coverage: Coverage compares the scored weight with the applicable weight.
method.coverage.low: Under 50% coverage, the domain stays not tested.
method.coverage.why: A score on too few tests would mislead.
method.global.title: Overall score
method.global.body: The overall score is the average of the scored domains, with equal weight.
method.global.eight: Eight main domains count, with the same weight.
method.global.aside: Reputation and availability are shown aside.
method.global.empty: With no scored domain, the overall score is not tested.
method.level.title: Levels
method.order.title: Order of fixes
method.order.body: Problems come first, then the points to improve.
method.order.tie: On a tie, the order follows the test identifier.
method.repro.title: Reproducibility
method.repro.body: The same answers give the same report.
method.proof: The report describes an observation. It is not a bailiff’s statement.
method.proof.link: The proof notices are on the verification page.
method.never.title: What we never do
method.never.lead: Out of respect for your servers and cybersecurity regulations, our testing is strictly bounded:
method.never.exploit: No intrusion attempts or security vulnerability exploitation.
method.never.bruteforce: No destructive testing, stress testing, or brute-force requests.
method.never.submit: No submission of contact forms or test shopping carts.
method.never.sell: No sale of your reports, emails, or audit data.
method.self.title: Transparency and self-audit
method.self.lead: Audigy applies all measured standards to its own platform:
method.self.privacy: Zero commercial trackers, zero third-party cookies before consent.
method.self.a11y: Accessible design (Atkinson Hyperlegible font, high contrast ratios).

priorities.why.dmarc: Protects your domain name from spoofing and ensures email deliverability.
priorities.why.spf: Officially declares which servers are authorized to send email from your domain.
priorities.why.dkim: Cryptographically signs your emails to prevent them from landing in spam.
priorities.why.hsts: Forces browsers to use an encrypted HTTPS connection and prevents interception.
priorities.why.https: Guarantees confidentiality and integrity of data exchanged with visitors.
priorities.why.xcto: Prevents browsers from guessing file types, blocking content-sniffing attacks.
priorities.why.frames: Prevents embedding your pages into invisible malicious frames (clickjacking).
priorities.why.csp: Restricts allowed script sources and prevents malicious code injection.
priorities.why.images_poids: Oversized images drastically slow down rendering, especially on mobile devices.
priorities.why.images_dimensions: Specifying image width and height prevents annoying layout shifts during loading.
priorities.why.accessibilite: Allows visually impaired or keyboard-navigating users to use your site without barriers.
priorities.why.seo_title: The page title is the primary signal examined by search engines.
priorities.why.seo_description: The description entices searchers to click your link in Google results.
priorities.why.traceurs: Setting cookies before consent violates GDPR regulations and the ePrivacy directive.
priorities.why.compression: Enabling Gzip or Brotli compression reduces bandwidth and carbon footprint.
priorities.why.default: This improvement strengthens reliability, speed, and regulatory compliance.
